verses.1: And Ahaz had seventy sons in Samaria. He wrote records, and he sent them to the elders of Judah and to the wise men. Ahaz said:
verses.2: And now, as this book is presented to you, to your children, to you who are riders on horses and chariots, and to those who live in cities and towns.
verses.3: And when they saw the good and righteous among your people, you put them on the throne of their father’s house. But they fought against the house of your Lord.
verses.4: And they saw so much that they said, “Look! These two kings cannot stand before him. How can we stand before him?”
verses.5: And he sent out those who were in the house, and also those who were in the city, along with the elders and the wise men, to say to them, “Your servants are we. All that you command us to do shall be done. But I will not appoint a good man over you.”
verses.6: And he wrote a list for them again, saying, “If you are willing to listen to me, then come before me tomorrow. Seventy men from the king’s people will be chosen to lead these people. They will be trained to become leaders of the city.”
verses.7: And when the scribe came to them, they took the sons of the king and slaughtered seventy men. They placed their heads in containers, and then sent them to Yizraelah.
verses.8: And the angel came and told him, “Bring forth the heads of the king’s sons.” He said, “Put them in two groups, and open the gate until tomorrow.”
verses.9: And in the morning, he went out and stood up. He said to all the righteous people, “Look, I am tied to my pillar, and I will kill him. But who will kill all those people?”
verses.10: Know this: The land that God spoke of regarding the house of Avah will not be destroyed. God did what He said through His servant Elijah.
verses.11: And He gathered all those who remained in the house of Ahab in Israel, along with all their leaders, priests, and officials. But He didn’t leave behind any survivors.
verses.12: And he got up, went out, and walked along the path leading to the house of the wicked.
verses.13: And he found his brothers, Ahaziah’s brothers, who were kings of Judah. He asked, “Who are you?” They replied, “We are Ahaziah’s brothers. We will go to see the king and the nobles.”
verses.14: And they said, “Let them be taken alive. They will be taken alive and slaughtered at the pit of judgment. Forty-two men will be killed, and not a single one will be left alive.”
verses.15: He went there and found Jehondab, son of Rekhav. He blessed him and said to him, “May your heart be as pure as mine is.” Jehondab replied, “I will give you my hand.” So he gave his hand to him, and they both got into the chariot.
verses.16: And he said to me, “Come to me. See how I am anxious for the Lord’s sake. Then he rode him on his back.”
verses.17: And Shomeron came and took all those who remained to Ahava in Shomeron, until they were destroyed, as Jehovah had commanded Eliyah.
verses.18: And Jehu gathered all the people together and said to them, “Ahab has served the king. But Jehu will serve us much more.”
verses.19: And now, all the prophets of the king, all his servants and priests, called upon me. But I will not be disturbed. For this great offering I made for the king, none of them will live. They acted in accordance with my commands, just to take away the servants of the king from their positions.
verses.20: And Yehu said, “Let it be holy for the husbandman.” And they called out in praise.
verses.21: And Jehu sent out his messengers throughout all Israel. All the servants of the king came forward; not a single person remained who did not come. They entered the king’s house, and they filled the house with people from every side.
verses.22: And he said to those who were on the throne: “Let there be a cry out for help from all the servants of the Lord.” And so, a cry of distress was raised among them.
verses.23: And Jehoham and Jehozadak, sons of Rekhab, came into the house of the king. They said to the servants of the king, “Search carefully, and see if there isn’t anyone among your people who is a servant of Jehovah. For only the servants of the king are worthy to serve.”
verses.24: And they came to perform sacrifices and offerings. There, in the wilderness, there was a man who stood there. The man said, “The one who is taken from among the people that I bring before you, his soul shall be under my control.”
verses.25: And he did what was necessary to carry out his plan. He said, “Let the birds go.” So the birds went away. No one should come near them. They flew away along the path of destruction. Then they went on their way until they reached the city of Beit HaBaal.
verses.26: And they took out the contents of the man’s house and burned them.
verses.27: And they destroyed the husband’s dwelling, and they also destroyed his house. They left it in a state of ruin until today.
verses.28: And Yehu saved the man from Israel.
verses.29: Only the sins of Jerubbaal, son of Nebat, who led Israel astray, were not forgiven by Jehovah. He also punished those golden calves that were in Bethel and Dan.
verses.30: And the LORD said to him, “Because you have done what is right in my eyes, just as all that is in my heart you have done for Ahau’s house. So, fifty sons of Reuben will sit on the throne of Israel.”
verses.31: And he did not keep the commandments of Jehovah, the God of Israel, with all his heart. He did not refrain from his sins, the sins that Jeroboam had committed and which led Israel astray.
verses.32: In those days, Jehovah began to divide Israel into tribes. Hazael ruled over all the borders of Israel.
verses.33: From the east side of the sun, all of the land of Gilad, Gad, and Manasye is covered with clouds. This land includes the region along the Arnon River, Gilad, and Bashan.
verses.34: And all the words of Jehova, and everything he did, and all his miracles—all these are recorded in the book of the days of Israel’s kings.
verses.35: And Jehoahaz lay down with his fathers. They buried him in Samaria. And Jehoahaz’s son, Jehoash, became king after him.
verses.36: And in the days when Jehova ruled over Israel, there were forty years and a hundred and fifty years of reign in Shemot.
